newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania retires Ceausescu's personal physician.
newsitem.headline: Romania retires Ceausescu's personal physician.

text.p: Romania's Health Ministry on Monday pensioned off Iulian Mincu, dictator Nicolae Ceausescu's personal physician who told Romanians meat was bad for them during severe shortages of the 1980s.
"Professor Iulian Mincu is to retire as head of the Institute for Nutrition and Metabolic Diseases as he has reached retirement age," a ministry statement said.
Mincu, a nutritionist, became notorious near the end of Ceausescu's 25-year rule as mastermind of the "rational nutrition programme" which denied meat and sweets to the country's 23 million people.
Even after Ceausescu's execution on Christmas Day 1989 he retained the favours of the ex-communists who took power and served as health minister from 1992 to 1996.

In the early 1980s, after Ceausescu ordered food and other goods to be exported to pay off Romania's external debt, Mincu told Romanians shivering in unheated flats and facing empty shops that meat was bad for their health.

He suggested Romanians issued half a kg (one pound) of meat and 200 grams (half a pound) of butter per week were better off consuming large amounts of fish and vegetables as part of his "scientific feeding programme".
He gave the diabetic Ceausescu his last insulin injection hours before the dictator and his wife Elena fled Bucharest by helicopter during the December 1989 uprising.

During his tenure as health minister Mincu came under attack from doctors who blamed him for the disastrous state of Romania's health system. He was accused of failing to make use of World Bank credits intended to upgrade equipment and of stalling moves to privatise parts of the health system.

Mincu was replaced early last year, several months before centrists defeated ex-communists in a general election. His retirement was part of plans to lay off tens of thousands of doctors to cut costs and improve efficiency.
